turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Reasoning from device physics

**What the training data tells us about high-efficiency recipes (>19%):**

The top performers cluster tightly around a clear archetype:
- **Composition:** Triple/mixed-cation `FAMAPbBrI` or `CsFAMAPbBrI` — the ~1.5–1.6 eV mixed-halide bandgap, stabilized by Cs/MA, gives high Voc and Jsc with good crystallinity.
- **ETL:** planar `SnO2-c/np` or mesoporous `TiO2-c | TiO2-mp` — well-aligned conduction band, low hysteresis (SnO2).
- **HTL:** `Spiro-MeOTAD` (n-i-p) or `PTAA` (p-i-n) — deep HOMO for good hole selectivity; **interface passivation** additives (SrCl2, amine oxides, PEIA, OAI/DM) push efficiency to the very top (>20–23%).
- **Contact:** `Au` (n-i-p) — ideal work function, no reaction.
- **Process:** simple spin-coating of these mature stacks.

Failure modes to avoid: Sn-containing (oxidation, low Voc), Bi/Sb/Ge (wide/indirect gaps, low Jsc), pure-Br or Cs-only halides (high gap → low current), PEDOT:PSS (acidic, low Voc ceiling), carbon back-contacts on non-optimized stacks.

**Screening the pool for the winning archetype (mixed-cation Pb-halide + selective TL + passivation + Au):**

- **c099** — `FAMAPbBrI`, TiO2-c/mp, **Au-nw | Spiro-MeOTAD**, Au. The Au-nanowire/Spiro composite HTL enhances conductivity + collection; classic high-Voc n-i-p stack. Strong.
- **c019** — `FAMAPbBrI`, TiO2-c/mp, **DM**, Au. DM (dimethoxydiphenylamine spirobifluorene) is exactly the champion HTL from the 22.9% training row (OAI | DM). Excellent HOMO alignment.
- **c057** — `FAMAPbBrI`, TiO2-c/mp, **X25**, Au. Designer high-mobility HTL on the ideal absorber/ETL — matches the 20–21% family (LD22, SFXDAnCBZ, FDT class).
- **c047** — `FAMAPbBrI`, ITO/**SnO2-c**, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au. Exactly the 17.8–18.2% SnO2-c/Spiro/Au recipe; robust, low-hysteresis.
- **c015** — `CsFAMAPbBrI | (EPA)PbI`, TiO2-c/mp, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au. A **2D/3D passivation cap** on the best triple-cation stack — mirrors the top training entries with (PEI/oFPEA/OA) capping layers.

These five best replicate the physics of the >19% champions: optimal bandgap, selective well-aligned transport layers, an inert Au contact, and explicit interface passivation.

**Final: c019, c099, c015, c057, c047**
